strengths: The manuscript offers an informative proof of concept: learned reward uncertainty combined with robust planning can produce cautious behavior without explicitly designating a safe policy. This has an identifiable audience in robust reinforcement learning and AI safety.

The experiments generally support that limited claim. In the initial single-image task, 1-of-20 selects help on 89% of fashion images and 68% of letter images while retaining 96–99% digit accuracy. Comparisons with k=N help separate robustness from ensembling, and the context-dependent help task goes beyond learning one universally conservative action.

The training-data experiment usefully demonstrates a failure condition: increasing robustness does not reliably induce caution when the reward models have insufficient data. The continuing-MDP extension also provides theoretical substance through the performance-difference-lemma argument.

The main exposition is understandable, and the authors explicitly acknowledge known transitions, tabular policies, exact policy evaluation, and limitations of interpreting robustness as safety. These restrictions do not preclude publication of the demonstrated findings.
weaknesses: Necessary theoretical corrections: Appendix B’s probability argument contains reversed inequalities in Eqs. (11)–(13), and Eq. (13) lacks the negative exponent required for a concentration bound. The martingale argument should explicitly use expectations conditional on previous iterations. A standard one-sided Azuma–Hoeffding argument appears to recover the stated result, so these are localized corrections rather than a fundamental objection to the theorem.

Necessary claim clarification: Theorem 2 guarantees the best iterate and a uniformly sampled iterate, whereas experiments use the final iterate after 100 iterations. It does not establish convergence of the final iterate. The convergence wording should reflect this distinction; the reported learning curves provide empirical reassurance but do not close that theoretical gap.

Necessary reporting corrections: Appendix A says the all-images policy requests help for most letters, contradicting Section 4’s approximately 6% rate and Figure 8. The manuscript should also define the plotted uncertainty summaries and clarify that the ten MNIST and five gridworld repetitions reshuffle a fixed trained ensemble, rather than independently repeating the complete training procedure.

The evidence establishes behavioral caution within the constructed tasks, with substantial dependence on the evaluation regime: help selection on fashion images falls from 89% in the single-image regime to 29% in the all-images regime. Novel-state rewards are deliberately undefined, and the most robust driving policy nearly stops. Thus, these results provide limited evidence about useful safety gains or generalization to other kinds of novelty.

Optional improvements: Reporting driving progress alongside collisions, evaluating familiar-environment driving behavior, and directly examining ensemble disagreement would better explain the safety–utility tradeoff and proposed mechanism. Smaller-ensemble studies would help assess practicality. These extensions are not prerequisites for the paper’s limited proof-of-concept contribution.
